status: Authored checklist, not legal advice. Each requirement quotes its source. Not reviewed by a regulatory professional.

sources.title: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, section 524B (21 U.S.C. 360n-2), Ensuring cybersecurity of devices
FDA guidance: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions (issued February 3, 2026; GUI00001825)

scope.quote: a person, including a manufacturer, who submits a premarket application or submission under any of the following pathways—510(k), PMA, PDP, De Novo, or HDE—for a device that meets the definition of a “cyber device,” as defined in section 524B(c), is required to include such information as FDA may require

internetCapableMedia.quote: FDA considers devices that include any of the following features to have the ability to connect to the internet. The list below is illustrative, not exhaustive: Network, server, or Cloud Service Provider connections; Radio-frequency communications (e.g., Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth, Bluetooth Low Energy); Magnetic inductive communications; and Hardware connectors capable of connecting to the internet (e.g., USB, ethernet
internetCapableMedia.note: Mapping the tool's link types onto FDA's list is this tool's own reading. NFC and proprietary RF are treated as radio-frequency communications.

requirements.title: Postmarket vulnerability plan, including coordinated disclosure
requirements.suggestedFix: Write the plan for monitoring, identifying, and addressing vulnerabilities after market entry, with a coordinated vulnerability disclosure procedure. This tool does not produce it.
requirements.quote: submit to the Secretary a plan to monitor, identify, and address, as appropriate, in a reasonable time, postmarket cybersecurity vulnerabilities and exploits, including coordinated vulnerability disclosure and related procedures

requirements.title: Processes and procedures giving reasonable assurance the device is cybersecure
requirements.suggestedFix: Document the secure development processes and the update and patch process. The risk register here can feed that documentation but does not replace it.
requirements.quote: design, develop, and maintain processes and procedures to provide a reasonable assurance that the device and related systems are cybersecure

requirements.title: Software bill of materials
requirements.suggestedFix: Generate a software bill of materials covering commercial, open-source, and off-the-shelf components. This tool does not read or produce one.
requirements.quote: provide to the Secretary a software bill of materials, including commercial, open-source, and off-the-shelf software components

requirements.title: Threat modeling documentation
requirements.suggestedFix: Use the matched techniques, baseline threats, and risk register in this report as a first draft. Have a qualified reviewer complete and sign it.
requirements.quote: FDA recommends that premarket submissions include threat modeling documentation to demonstrate how the medical device system has been analyzed to identify potential security risks that could impact safety and effectiveness.

requirements.title: Rationale for the threat modeling method
requirements.suggestedFix: The method section of this report states the method used. Adapt it and say why it suits your device.
requirements.quote: Rationale for the methodology(ies) selected should be provided with the threat modeling documentation.

requirements.title: Stated assumptions about the system and environment of use
requirements.suggestedFix: List your assumptions about the environment of use, for example that networks the device touches are hostile. The tool cannot know them.
requirements.quote: State any assumptions about the medical device system or environment of use

requirements.title: Risk assessment based on exploitability
requirements.suggestedFix: The register lists a CVSS base vector where the catalog has one. Rows marked not scored need an exploitability assessment from you.
requirements.quote: security risk assessment processes focus on exploitability, or the ability to exploit vulnerabilities present within a device and/or system.

requirements.title: Four security architecture views, with diagrams and explanatory text
requirements.suggestedFix: The four views in this report are drafts drawn from your answers. Add the detail FDA's Appendix 2 asks for, and explanatory text for each.
requirements.quote: FDA recommends providing, at minimum, the following types of views in premarket submissions: Global System View; Multi-Patient Harm View; Updateability/Patchability View; and Security Use Case View(s).

requirements.title: Cybersecurity risks in the informed consent form
requirements.suggestedFix: Add the device's cybersecurity risks to the informed consent form.
requirements.quote: Inclusion of cybersecurity risks as part of informed consent form (21 CFR 50.25(a)(2) and 21 CFR 812.25(g));

requirements.title: Global, multi-patient, and updateability views
requirements.suggestedFix: Use the three views in this report as drafts and complete them for the investigational plan.
requirements.quote: Global, multi-patient and updateability/patchability views (21 CFR 812.25(c), (d));

requirements.title: Security use case views for functions with safety risks
requirements.suggestedFix: Use the security use case view in this report as a draft for safety-relevant functions such as implant programming.
requirements.quote: Security use case views for functionality with safety risks (e.g., implant programming) (21 CFR 812.25(c), (d));

requirements.title: Software bill of materials
requirements.suggestedFix: Generate a software bill of materials for the investigational device. This tool does not read or produce one.
requirements.quote: Software Bill of Materials (21 CFR 812.25(c), (d)); and

requirements.title: General labeling on connectivity, cybersecurity risks, and updates
requirements.suggestedFix: Describe the device's connectivity, its general cybersecurity risks, and how it is updated in the labeling.
requirements.quote: General labeling – connectivity and associated general cybersecurity risks, updateability/process (21 CFR 812.25(f)).
